destination_record.tagline: Sun, sand and Portuguese-era heritage on India's west coast, from lively Baga to peaceful Palolem.

on.places: Baga, Calangute, Anjuna, Colva, Palolem, Old Goa, Fontainhas, Dudhsagar Falls
on.activities: Dry, sunny weather with cooler evenings. Beach days, water sports, sunset river cruises, Dudhsagar jeep safaris, heritage walks and markets; Christmas and New Year are the busiest weeks, so book early.

off.places: Old Goa, Fontainhas, spice plantations, Ayurveda and spa stays, the green Goan countryside
off.activities: Monsoon with heavy rain and a rough sea; swimming and water sports are usually closed and many beach shacks shut. Lush scenery, lower prices and relaxed spa and heritage stays, with access to Dudhsagar usually restricted.

mid.places: Baga, Calangute, Colva, Palolem, Old Goa, Panjim
mid.activities: Warmer and more humid, with calm seas and fewer crowds. Good for beach days, church and city visits and spa breaks; March to May can be hot, so plan sightseeing for mornings and evenings.

profile.overview:
Goa is India's smallest state and its most relaxed holiday coast, with long Arabian Sea beaches, palm-fringed villages and four centuries of Portuguese heritage left in its churches, forts and painted houses. North Goa is lively, with Baga, Calangute and Anjuna beaches, beach shacks, markets and hilltop forts. South Goa is calmer, with the wide sands of Colva and the crescent bay at Palolem.

Beyond the beaches there is plenty to do: the UNESCO-listed churches of Old Goa, the Latin Quarter of Fontainhas in Panjim, an evening cruise on the Mandovi river, spice plantations in the hills and a jeep ride to Dudhsagar Falls. It suits families, friends, couples and senior parents alike. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the trip around you.

facts.climate: About 22°C to 35°C, warm and humid; heavy monsoon rain from June to September, with the best weather from November to February
facts.flight_time: About 1 hr 30 min to 2 hr from Chennai and about 2 hr 45 min from Delhi by direct flight, to Dabolim (GOI) or Mopa (GOX); long-distance trains reach Madgaon

reasons.title: Beaches for every mood
reasons.text: Lively Baga and Calangute in the north, quiet Palolem and Colva in the south, so you can choose your pace.

reasons.title: Portuguese-era heritage
reasons.text: Old Goa's grand churches and Panjim's Fontainhas give the coast a history that few beach destinations can match.

reasons.title: Easy to reach
reasons.text: Direct flights from Chennai and other metros, two airports and a railhead at Madgaon make it simple to plan, even for a long weekend.

reasons.title: Rivers, waterfalls and spice hills
reasons.text: Mandovi cruises, spice plantations and the Dudhsagar jeep ride add variety to the sea and sand.

reasons.title: Good for all ages
reasons.text: Gentle beaches, short drives and plenty of hotels and resorts suit families, couples and senior parents.

attractions.title: Baga and Calangute beaches
attractions.text: North Goa's busiest stretch of sand, with beach shacks, sunset views and water sports in the season.

attractions.title: Anjuna Beach and Chapora Fort
attractions.text: A rocky, laid-back beach and the hilltop fort above Vagator with sweeping views of the coast.

attractions.title: Fort Aguada
attractions.text: A 17th-century Portuguese fort and lighthouse at Candolim, overlooking the sea.

attractions.title: Old Goa churches
attractions.text: The Basilica of Bom Jesus, Se Cathedral and the Church of St Francis of Assisi, part of a UNESCO World Heritage site.

attractions.title: Fontainhas, Panjim
attractions.text: A Latin Quarter of narrow lanes, colourful Portuguese-style houses and the whitewashed Chapel of St Sebastian.

attractions.title: Dudhsagar Falls
attractions.text: A tiered waterfall in the Western Ghats, reached by jeep from the Mollem and Collem side during the open season.

attractions.title: Palolem Beach
attractions.text: A calm crescent bay in South Goa, framed by palms and hills, popular for easy swimming and sunsets.

attractions.title: Colva Beach
attractions.text: A long, wide beach in South Goa with a relaxed family feel and plenty of cafes.

experiences.title: Sunset cruise on the Mandovi
experiences.text: An evening river cruise from Panjim, typically with music and a cultural programme on board.

experiences.title: Dudhsagar jeep safari
experiences.text: A bumpy ride through forest and stream crossings to one of India's best-known waterfalls.

experiences.title: Spice plantation visit
experiences.text: A guided walk among pepper, cardamom, cashew and vanilla, usually followed by a Goan meal.

experiences.title: Water sports and dolphin trips
experiences.text: Parasailing, jet skiing and banana boat rides at the northern beaches, and boat trips at Palolem, in the open season.

experiences.title: Heritage walk through Fontainhas
experiences.text: An unhurried walk past Portuguese-era houses, small cafes and art galleries.

experiences.title: Sunsets at a beach shack
experiences.text: A simple but memorable evening of fresh seafood, cold drinks and the sea turning gold.

food.title: Goan fish curry and rice
food.text: A coconut-based curry with a tangy kick, eaten with rice at almost every local restaurant.

food.title: Prawn balchao and seafood grills
food.text: Spicy pickled prawns and freshly grilled catch of the day at beach shacks.

food.title: Bebinca
food.text: A rich, layered coconut and egg dessert that is a Goan Christmas classic and available all year.

food.title: Poi and bhaji
food.text: Soft local bread served with a lightly spiced potato curry, a favourite breakfast.

food.title: Vegetarian and Jain meals
food.text: Vegetarian thalis are easy to find, and we can arrange Jain and Indian meal options with advance notice.

tips.title: Dress modestly in churches
tips.text: Cover shoulders and knees when visiting the churches and temples of Old Goa.

tips.title: Respect the sea
tips.text: Swim only in flagged areas near lifeguards, and avoid the water when red flags are up or the sea is rough.

tips.title: Plan around the monsoon
tips.text: From June to September the sea is rough, swimming and water sports are usually closed and many beach shacks shut.

tips.title: Book early for Christmas and New Year
tips.text: Late December is the busiest and most expensive time, so reserve hotels and transfers well ahead.

tips.title: Drive carefully
tips.text: If you hire a scooter, wear a helmet and carry your licence, and never drink and drive.

tips.title: Carry sun protection
tips.text: The coastal sun is strong all year, so pack sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses and a reusable water bottle.

travel_info.visa: Indian citizens need no visa to visit Goa. Carry a valid government photo ID, such as Aadhaar, passport, driving licence or voter ID, for flights, trains and hotel check-in. No special permit is needed for the standard beach, heritage and Dudhsagar sightseeing in our packages; we arrange permits and confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations. Drink bottled or filtered water, use sunscreen and mosquito repellent, and carry your regular medicines. Take care in the sea, as currents can be strong, and avoid swimming in the monsoon.
travel_info.money: UPI and cards work in most hotels, restaurants and shops, but carry some cash for beach shacks, taxis, markets and small purchases. ATMs are widely available in the main beach towns. Tipping 5 to 10 per cent for good service is customary.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Goa?
faqs.a: Three to four nights covers the main beaches and Old Goa. Five to six nights lets you add South Goa and Dudhsagar at an easy pace.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Goa?
faqs.a: November to February is dry, sunny and the busiest season. October and March to May are warmer with lower prices, and June to September is the monsoon, when the sea is rough and water sports are closed.

faqs.q: Which is better, North Goa or South Goa?
faqs.a: North Goa has the livelier beaches, forts, markets and nightlife. South Goa is quieter and more spacious, which suits families, couples and senior travellers. Many of our trips combine both.

faqs.q: Is Goa good for families and senior parents?
faqs.a: Yes. Distances are short, hotels have pools and many beaches have gentle waters. We can plan relaxed days and arrange vegetarian and Jain meal options.

faqs.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faqs.a: Dabolim (GOI) in the south and Mopa (GOX) in the north both serve Goa. Madgaon is the main railhead. We plan the transfer from whichever arrival point you use.
The jeep safari usually runs in the dry season and is restricted during the heavy monsoon. We confirm the current position at booking.

group_trips.title: Goa Beaches, Old Goa and Palolem Group Trip
group_trips.summary: Six days across North and South Goa with Baga, Anjuna and Chapora Fort, the Old Goa churches, Fontainhas, a Mandovi cruise and Palolem Beach, travelling in a small group.
group_trips.overview:
This group trip covers both sides of Goa over five nights, three in North Goa and two in South Goa. You see the beaches and forts of the north, the UNESCO-listed churches of Old Goa and the painted lanes of Fontainhas, with an evening river cruise on the Mandovi.

You then travel south, stopping at a spice plantation near Ponda on the way, and spend a day at the crescent bay of Palolem. A trip captain travels with the group, and Indian meal options are available on request.

The pace is easy, with free time on most days, which suits families, friends travelling together and senior parents.

honeymoon_trips.title: Goa Honeymoon: Beach Sunsets, River Cruise and Palolem Bay
honeymoon_trips.summary: Five unhurried nights for two in North and South Goa, with a flower welcome, a Mandovi sunset cruise, a couples spa session, a candlelight dinner by the sea and a quiet day at Palolem.
honeymoon_trips.overview:
This private honeymoon pairs the beaches of North Goa with the calmer bays of the south: three nights in the north and two in the south. You travel by private car throughout, start most mornings late and keep every evening for each other.

North Goa brings Fort Aguada, Anjuna Beach, the hilltop views from Chapora Fort and the churches of Old Goa. In Panjim you wander through Fontainhas and then board a sunset cruise on the Mandovi river. In the south you spend time at Colva and a slow day at Palolem Beach.

Expect a flower welcome or bed decoration on arrival, a couples spa session and a candlelight dinner by the sea, all subject to availability. Tell us your wedding date at booking and we will pass it to the hotels.

Fort Aguada, Anjuna Beach and Chapora Fort at a gentle pace

custom_trips.title: Goa Beach Saver: Three Nights in North Goa
custom_trips.summary: A value three-night North Goa break with Baga, Calangute and Anjuna beaches, Chapora Fort, Old Goa and Fontainhas.
custom_trips.overview:
This budget-friendly break keeps everything simple, with three nights in one comfortable hotel near Calangute and Baga, so you unpack once. Two days of sightseeing cover the best-known beaches and forts of North Goa, the churches of Old Goa and the lanes of Fontainhas in Panjim.

The remaining time is yours for the beach, the pool and the shacks. It suits friends, young families and first-time visitors who want Goa at a sensible price.
highlights: Three nights in one hotel, with no packing and unpacking
Baga, Calangute and Anjuna beaches
Chapora Fort viewpoint above Vagator
Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral in Old Goa
Walk through Fontainhas, Panjim

itinerary.title: Arrival in Goa | Baga Beach
itinerary.description:
Arrive in Goa and meet our representative at the airport or railway station.
Transfer to your hotel in the Calangute and Baga area and check in.
Spend the evening on Baga Beach.
Overnight stay in North Goa.

itinerary.title: North Goa Beaches and Chapora Fort
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive along the coast to Calangute, Anjuna and Vagator.
Visit Chapora Fort for views over the sea.
Return to the hotel and enjoy a free evening.
Overnight stay in North Goa.

itinerary.title: Old Goa | Fontainhas | Free Evening
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to Old Goa to see the Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral.
Continue to Panjim and walk through the lanes of Fontainhas.
Return to the hotel for a free evening.
Overnight stay in North Goa.

itinerary.title: Departure from Goa
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel.
Transfer to the airport or Madgaon railway station for your journey home.

custom_trips.title: Goa Family Holiday: Dudhsagar, Spice Plantation and Beaches
custom_trips.summary: Five nights in North and South Goa for families, with a Dudhsagar Falls jeep ride, a spice plantation, a Mandovi cruise, Old Goa and easy beach days.
custom_trips.overview:
This family holiday mixes easy beach time with the experiences that children and grandparents enjoy together. You spend three nights in North Goa and two in South Goa, with short drives and one main outing each day.

Highlights are a jeep ride to Dudhsagar Falls, a guided walk through a spice plantation, a family cruise on the Mandovi and the churches of Old Goa, with Colva and Palolem for relaxed time by the sea. Dudhsagar access depends on the season, so this trip is best from October to May.
highlights: Jeep safari to Dudhsagar Falls, subject to season
Guided walk through a spice plantation near Ponda
Family-friendly cruise on the Mandovi river
Old Goa churches and a short walk in Fontainhas
Easy beach days at Baga, Colva and Palolem

itinerary.title: Arrival in Goa | Evening at Leisure
itinerary.description:
Arrive in Goa and meet our representative at the airport or railway station.
Transfer to your hotel in North Goa and check in.
Spend the evening at the pool or on the beach.
Overnight stay in North Goa.

itinerary.title: Spice Plantation | Dudhsagar Falls
itinerary.description:
After an early breakfast, drive towards the Western Ghats.
Visit a spice plantation near Ponda for a guided walk and lunch.
Continue to the Mollem and Collem side for a jeep ride to Dudhsagar Falls, subject to season and conditions.
Return to your North Goa hotel in the evening.
Overnight stay in North Goa.

itinerary.title: Old Goa | Fontainhas | Mandovi Cruise
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to Old Goa to see the Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral.
Walk through the lanes of Fontainhas in Panjim.
In the evening, board a river cruise on the Mandovi.
Return to your hotel after the cruise.
Overnight stay in North Goa.

itinerary.title: Beach Morning | Transfer to South Goa
itinerary.description:
Enjoy a relaxed morning at the pool or at Baga Beach.
After lunch, check out and drive to South Goa.
Check in at your hotel in the Colva or Benaulim area and visit Colva Beach in the evening.
Overnight stay in South Goa.

itinerary.title: Palolem Beach Day
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to Palolem Beach in Canacona, around an hour away.
Spend the day on the beach at an easy pace, with optional boat trips subject to season and sea conditions.
Return to your hotel in the evening.
Overnight stay in South Goa.

itinerary.title: Departure from Goa
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel.
Transfer to the airport or Madgaon railway station for your journey home.
